steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Place ribs in two 10x15-inch roasting pans. Pour water and red wine vinegar into a bowl; stir to mix and pour over ribs. Cover the pans with foil and bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes. Baste the ribs with juices halfway through cooking.

Meanwhile, make the BBQ sauce: Mix ketchup, water, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, butter, brown sugar, hot pepper sauce, and salt together in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until sauce has thickened, about 1 hour.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat.

Lightly oil preheated grill. Transfer ribs from the oven to the grill, discarding cooking liquid. Grill over medium heat for 15 minutes, turning ribs once. Baste ribs generously with some of the BBQ sauce, and grill for 5 minutes. Turn ribs, baste again with BBQ sauce, and grill 5 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Southern Grilled BBQ Ribs
raw_recipe.description: These grilled BBQ ribs are baked, then cooked on the grill and basted with a homemade tangy BBQ sauce until tender and juicy.
raw_recipe.name: Southern Grilled BBQ Ribs

review.reviewBody: I've been doing ribs by this method for years and you appreciate it even more in winter where grilling 5-6 hr ribs is not an option. (In winter, you would finish this recipe off topped with the sauce in a 450 degree oven instead of on the grill.) A few suggestions from my experience. I add a bit of liquid smoke to the vinegar mixture so that it permeates the ribs when baking (also throw in a few cloves of garlic, bay leaf, salt and pepper). I take off the foil after 45 minutes of baking but continue baking until the yummy liquid evaporates(the flavor gets more concentrated in the meat that way). The beauty is that this step can be done even a few days ahead. When done baking, I just let the ribs cool and refrigerate until I need them. Then, just take out 1 hr before party/ dinner, baste generously w/sauce and grill/ bake until nice in color. Perfect for treating kids to their favorite dinner in the middle of the week even for a busy mom/ dad or for throwing a no hassle BBQ party.

I love this recipe and in the future would like to follow it more closely using baby back ribs. But I had over 5 lbs of large spare ribs and changed it up a bit. I cut into serving pieces and put them in 1 xlarge and 1 large size cooking bags with 1 T of flour in each bag. Poured the 2/3 cup wine vinegar and 1/3 cup water mixed together over the spare ribs distributing between the 2 cooking bags. Baked them in a 325 degree over for about 2 1/2 hours. Took all serving pieces out of the bags and placed them in a large casserole dish , poured popular store bought BBQ sauce over the spare ribs letting them marinate in the sauce for about 45 minutes. My husband put them on the grill about 4-5 minutes per side to Carmelize the sauce. They are pull off the bone tender and yummy.

Wow, these are so good and so easy! I used boneless pork ribs and they turned out great! I only had to use one pan in the oven as they easily fit. I did cook in the oven an extra 15 - 30 minutes, just long enough for the barbecue sauce to simmer for an hour. The barbecue sauce was slightly thin for my tastes so next time I will simmer it with the lid off. My husband who is very picky, couldn't get enough! They grilled up to perfection, I basted about every two minutes. Thank you, I plan on making these again and again.

Superb and traditional, "fall off the bone" if you slow oven roast and then char, ever so slightly, over a low layer of hot coals! We added wood chips on the coals to give an even more rustic flavor!!

I read the comment on doing this in winter. What about during the really hot days in the summer, when the last thing you want is to heat up inside with the oven. How about "baking" as directed, but on/in the grill at 350 degrees? Of course, finishing after on the grill according to the recipe. An option I might try.

Love them. Always a hit! I add a couple of bay leaves and some liquid sauce to the vinegar mixture for the oven. I make the sauce after putting the ribs in the oven so they cook longer than the 45 minutes suggested probably more like an hour and a half. We haven't done them on the grill but pour the sauce on top of the ribs and pop them back in the oven for 30 minutes or so. Excellent!

This is a great sauce. This is the second time I have made it and this time I added 2 Tablespoons of dehydrated onions. Made it even better. I left tthe lid off the sauce pot and simmered for 40 minutes. The sauce was a great consistency. Nice and thick. I will be using this often.

Everyone loved this recipe. I lived in Memphis TN for 23 years so I consider myself a bit of a rib connoisseur - these were excellent! It was raining so rather then finish them on the grill I cooked them in the oven as one reviewer suggested. If you prefer some extra kick to your ribs just add more hot sauce.

Melt in your mouth, fall off the bone, lip smackin good! I stuck with the original recipe except for the final cooking portion. I followed Gigi9801 directions by letting them marinate in the sauce after the initial cooking for an hour and a half. I finished them in the oven baking them covered for 45 min then uncovered them for additional 10 min on each side. I had lined my broiler pan bottom with foil so clean up was super easy too. Definitely a keeper.

I made these for a neighborhood rib cookoff and won 2nd place out of 13 entries. I hit the slabs with some salt and pepper and put a layer of onions, garlic and a few bay leaves on the racks before pouring the vinegar over them. I also added a few drops of liquid smoke to the vinegar and water at the suggestion of another review. Very good!
Precooked the ribs, then took them camping & finished them on the grill. Delicious! What about the BBQ sauce? We have leftover sauce. What else can it be used on?

We used baby back ribs. I left plenty of time for the ribs to soak in the vinegar and baste before even baking. The BBQ sauce is nothing like what you buy in the store, so get that out of your head. It does not become thick like ketchup or BBQ. I typically par boil my ribs or just put in a slow cooker. Baking them came out better than I thought. They were tender (not fall-off-the-bone tender) and flavorful. I had also seasoned the ribs prior to pouring the vinegar over them. Salt, pepper, onion salt, garlic salt.
I added some liquid smoke to the vinegar mix and the bbq sauce. Gives it the been on the smoker all day flavor.

I didn’t make this recipe, but use one that’s very close. What is important to me is that the cook was wise to choose a recipe that’s so easy and quick. After following her lead, anyone is wasting time standing over a grill for 5-6 hrs!
Sounds great, more to follow and I have some ribs to try…..Although we do a recipe for ribs so you must eat the meat on the bone and we love it that way.
